# Field Headsets
Headsets are the standard radio for ground forces.
Every soldier gets one at issue. Keep it worn and know which radio keys it has.
## Named Nets
Use [color=#3FCF8E]:h[/color] to talk on your headset default net.
Most headsets also carry other keyed nets. Examine your headset to see which nets it has and which letter each one uses.
Examples: - [color=#3FCF8E]:v[/color] for command, if your headset has command. - [color=#3FCF8E]:a[/color] for Alpha, if your headset has Alpha.
Named nets are secured by keys loaded into the headset.
If your headset does not have the key, you cannot hear or speak on that net.
Do not remove keys unless ordered.
## Range and Relays
Combat nets — squad, command, intel and JTAC — only exist where something anchors them. Without coverage they are [bold]dead air[/bold], not unlimited:
- A powered [textlink="AN/PRC-117G" link="AU14CommsANPRC"] worn by a [bold]trained operator[/bold] (RTO, command, or the platoon sergeant) — on anyone else's back the pack relays nothing. - A planted retrans station. - A fixed [bold]comms array[/bold] (shipboard, powered) or [bold]antenna mast[/bold] (command post). Destroy the enemy's array and their base goes deaf.
Support nets such as MILP and colony channels are not relay-gated and work everywhere.
Stock relay range:
[bold]Distance from Radio[/bold]
[bold]Signal[/bold]
0 to 30 tiles
Clean send and receive.
30 to 45 tiles
Light garble.
Past 45 tiles
No relay signal.
These figures assume normal transmit power and a stock whip antenna.
Transmit power and antenna change the relay range. A stationary mast reaches much further. Low power reaches less. CP antenna masts cover roughly 75 tiles and shipboard comms arrays cover the whole ship.
If nothing anchors your net on the map, the net is dead until coverage is restored.
Stay near the RTO if you need reliable comms.
## Talking Up the Chain
Squad leader headsets carry the squad net and JTAC — [bold]not[/bold] the command net. The squad's voice to command is the RTO's manpack: stand next to the RTO (or a planted pack), alt-click them and [bold]Take Handset[/bold], then transmit with [color=#3FCF8E]:r[/color]. The cord reaches about 2 tiles — walk away and it yanks out of your hand.
You go on air under your own callsign, so command hears "ALPHA 6", not the RTO. This is the intended way for a squad leader to request fires, report to command, or take orders — keep your RTO alive and keep them close.
## Jamming
Enemy jammers affect headsets in two ways.
If you are inside a jammer field, your outgoing headset transmissions are blocked.
Move out of the field before calling for help.
Incoming traffic near a jammer becomes garbled. The closer you are to the jammer, the worse it gets.
Direct frequencies degrade the same way.
The AN/PRC can keep transmitting from inside a jammer field when using FH mode. Normal headsets cannot.
## Direct Frequency Tuning
Some headsets can tune one extra direct frequency.
Use [color=#3FCF8E]:x[/color] to transmit on it.
Direct frequency traffic: - Does not need a tower. - Does not need a named net. - Does not need an encryption key. - Works with anyone tuned to the same number.
To tune: - Right-click the headset. - Select [bold]Tune Frequency[/bold]. - Enter a frequency from [color=#3FCF8E]30.000[/color] to [color=#3FCF8E]87.999[/color] MHz.
Both formats work: - [color=#3FCF8E]30750[/color] - [color=#3FCF8E]30.750[/color]
The headset must be worn in your ears to transmit or receive.
## Direct Frequency Range
[bold]Distance[/bold]
[bold]Signal[/bold]
0 to 30 tiles
Clean.
30 to 50 tiles
Light garble.
Past 50 tiles
No signal.
An AN/PRC can bridge direct frequency traffic if the same frequency is loaded in one of its slots.
Both users must be within [bold]50 tiles[/bold] of the radio.
## Clearing Direct Frequency
To stop using the tuned frequency:
- Right-click the headset. - Select [bold]Clear Tuned Frequency[/bold].
Some headsets also have [bold]Reset to Default Frequency[/bold] if they shipped with a preset.
## Common Problems
[bold]Problem[/bold]
[bold]Fix[/bold]
[bold]No frequency set[/bold] when using [color=#3FCF8E]:x[/color]
Tune the headset first.
Only garble on a named net
You may be at relay edge, near a jammer, or near a transmitter affected by jamming.
Pure static while using an AN/PRC
The AN/PRC may be missing the matching COMSEC fill.
Cannot hear a named net
Check that your headset has the key for that net.
Nobody hears [color=#3FCF8E]:x[/color]
Check that both users are tuned to the exact same frequency and are in range.
Headsets do not use fill cards.
Fill cards are only for the AN/PRC.
